newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stals predicts big fall in S.Africa Q3 c/a deficit.
newsitem.headline: Stals predicts big fall in S.Africa Q3 c/a deficit.

text.p: Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Friday the economic position in South Africa was stabilising and the current account deficit would have narrowed sharply in the third quarter.
However, he cautioned that last month's sharp fall in the rand had distorted the situation again.

"The preliminary estimate that everybody can make at this stage on the current account in the third quarter is for a substantial decline in the deficit -- a very substantial decline in the seasonally adjusted annualised rate of the current account deficit," he said.

"The third quarter statistics will provide a lot of evidence of a stabilisation process that has started to work, that the balance of payments has started improving, that foreign reserves were not under that much pressure and the foreign exchange rate was a little more stable.
"The developments in October upset the whole programme again. Now the October figures will be completely distorted by the decline in the value of the rand."

South Africa's current account deficit sank to 4.6 billion rand in the second quarter of 1996 from 2.3 billion in the first quarter, but many economists believe the position has since improved as a weak rand stimulates exports and curbs imports.
The Reserve Bank is due to publish its next Quarterly Bulletin containing third quarter figures on December 5.
